paragraphs: Meboar baggemara ubeposeqam hoil vehayyayin hu chashub sheggorem beraka leatzmo shemmebarekin alayv "bore peri haggapen" bekamma meqomot beqiddush vehabdala ubirkat hammazon velel pesach veerusin venissuin umila "p sheen tzerikin lishtiyyato veen teebin elayv, lepikak eno nechshab tapel lappat lehippater bebirkato mibberaka rishona shehi bore peri haggapen, "p shettapel eleha lehippater bebirkat hammazon mibberaka acharona, lepi sheeno gorem leatzmo beraka acharona ella beraka rishona lebaddah shebbishbilah hu iqqar habaat hakkos bekol debarim hannizkarim shetteunin kos, velaken hayyayin "p shebba lishtoto tok hasseuda mebarek alayv bore peri haggepen veeno niptar bebirkat happat, "p sheshshotehu haadam kede lishrot haakila shebbemeayv vahare zeh kidbarim habbaim mechamat hasseuda betok hasseuda shenniptarim bimqom happat, mikkol maqom hoil vehayyayin hu chashub sheggorem beraka leatzmo bekamma meqomot hannizkarim leel "p sheen tzerikin lishtiyyato ukemo shebbearnu, al ken eno tapel lappat, mah sheen ken shear okalim umashqim habbaim betok hasseuda mechamat hasseuda shennitpalim lepet en tzerikin beraka vekaasher nibaram beezrat hashshem, vekol zeh meporash yotze beshulchan aruk haggaon rabbenu zalman za"l siman q"d seip :

clarification.explanation: Wine is especially significant in that it generates its own berachah (Borei peri hagafen) in a number of places — Kiddush, Havdalah, Birkat HaMazon, the night of Pesach, betrothal and marriage, and circumcision — even though one does not need to drink it and does not crave it. Therefore wine is not considered secondary to bread and is not exempted by the berachah of Hamotzi (the opening berachah), even though it is exempted by the concluding berachah (Birkat HaMazon), because wine does not generate its own concluding berachah — only its own opening berachah, for whose sake the cup is brought in all those matters. Therefore, even if one drinks wine during the meal, one recites Borei peri hagafen over it, and it is not exempted by the berachah on bread — unlike other foods and drinks that come on account of the meal, which are exempted by the berachah on bread.
takeaways: One recites Borei peri hagafen over wine on its own even during the meal, because it "generates its own berachah" (at Kiddush, Havdalah, etc.).
Only its opening berachah stands on its own; its concluding berachah is indeed exempted by Birkat HaMazon.

paragraphs: Hayyayin qana od chashibut umaala shehu poter kol mine mashqin, lepikak im berek al hayyayin en tzarik lebarek al shear mashqin dehayyayin poter kol mine mashqin ben bishat seuda ben bishar peamim, lepi shehayyayin hu iqqar mashqeh vehu rosh lekol mine mashqin ulekak hu iqqar leinyan beraka vekullan tepelim elayv, vehu sheyyihyu hammashqin lepanayv beshaa sheyyebarek al hayyayin o sheyyihyeh dato alehem, vaapillu eno qobea atzmo lishtot yayin, ella shoteh yayin meat derek aray letzorek mitzva vekayyotze, veshoteh aach"k mashqin harbeh - niptarin bebirkat hayyayin im haya dato alehem, abal im lo qaba atzmo lishtiyya ella sheshshoteh meat derek aray velo haya dato al mashqin acherim enam niptarim bebirkat hayyayin:

Laken tzerikin lehizzaher keshemmeqaddeshin beshabbat al hayyayin im rotzeh lishtot mayim o shear mashqin achar haqqiddush qodem birkat hammotzi tzarik sheyyihyu hammayim lepanayv o sheyyekavven alehem, veaz en tzarik lebarek al hammayim o shear mashqin, gam nakon lehazhir zeh hashshoteh mayim ben qiddush lebirkat hammotzi shello yishteh rebiit, kede shello yitchayyeb bibraka acharona veyikkanes bimbuka shel hammachaloqet deyesh omerim shetztzarik lebarek beraka acharona veen birkat hammazon poteret hammayim sheshshata qodem hammotzi, veyesh omerim sheen tzarik lebarek, veal ken tob lizzaher shello yishteh rebiit, umihu im taa veshata rebiit yebarek beraka acharona al hammayim qodem hammotzi, yaan deap al gab deyesh choleqin mikkol maqom sebara zo iqqar, mippene dekak hi hahaskamat rabbenu haggadol haari"y za"l asher tzapa berucha haqqodesh bammetzach rabbenu mh"r chayyim veyittol za"l bepaam achat sheshshata rebiit mayim qodem hammazon velo berak beraka acharona, vehokichu al zot vekannizkar beshaar taame hammitzot parashat eqeb yeuyyan sham, v"g dehay ubda derabbenu mh"r chayyim veyittol za"l shehubea beshaar taame hammitzot hannizkar epshar lihyot dibchol hava, mikkol maqom nireh dehu haddin bisudat shabbat deit bah qiddush name dina haki ledaat rabbenu haggadol haari"y za"l, vekaasher hokachti uberarti zot bsh"q mqbtzyl bs"d veayyen leharab birke yosep za"l siman q"d seip qatan b' yeuyyan sham:

clarification.explanation:
Wine has an additional virtue: it exempts all other types of beverages. Therefore, one who recites a berachah over wine need not recite a berachah over other beverages (whether during the meal or not at the time of a meal), because wine is the primary beverage and all other beverages are secondary to it. The condition for this: the other beverages must be before him at the time of the berachah over the wine, or he must intend them explicitly. Even one who does not set himself to drink wine, but drinks a little wine casually (for example, for the sake of a mitzvah), and afterward drinks a great deal of other beverages — those beverages are exempted by the berachah on the wine if he intended them; but if he did not set himself to drink and did not intend the other beverages, they are not exempted.
Therefore, one who recites Kiddush over wine on Shabbat and wishes afterward to drink water or another beverage before the berachah of Hamotzi must have the water before him at the time of the berachah on the wine, or intend it, and then he need not recite a separate berachah over it. It is also good to be careful not to drink a revi'it of water between Kiddush and Hamotzi, so as not to enter into doubt as to whether one is obligated in a concluding berachah over that water (there is a dispute: some say one is obligated, since Birkat HaMazon does not exempt it, and some say one is not obligated). And if one nevertheless erred and drank a revi'it of water before Hamotzi, he should recite a concluding berachah over it (Borei nefashot rabbot) before Hamotzi — for such is the ruling of our teacher the Ari, may his memory be blessed: it is told that the Ari perceived with divine inspiration that his disciple Rabbeinu Chaim Vital had once drunk a revi'it of water before Birkat HaMazon without reciting a concluding berachah, and rebuked him for this. The Ben Ish Chai explains that this law applies also to a Shabbat meal that includes Kiddush, and not only on a weekday.
takeaways: The berachah on wine exempts all other beverages, provided they are before him at the time of the berachah or he intends them.
At Shabbat Kiddush, if one wishes to drink water before Hamotzi, it is best to intend it in the berachah on the wine, and to avoid drinking a full revi'it so as not to enter into doubt.
If one nevertheless drank a revi'it of water before Hamotzi, he recites a concluding berachah over it, as the Ari, may his memory be blessed, instructed.

paragraphs: Yayin shellipne hammazon kegon haqqiddush sheomerim bimqom seuda poter hayyayin shebbetok hammazon im haya bedato lishtot betok hasseuda, veim en darko bekak venimlak verotzeh lishtot, o shennatenu lo acherim tzarik lachazor ulebarek:

clarification.explanation: Wine drunk before the meal (such as Kiddush recited in place of a meal) also exempts wine drunk during the meal, if he had intended to drink it during the meal. But if it is not his usual practice and he changes his mind and wishes to drink, or others served it to him, he must recite the berachah again.
takeaways: Kiddush exempts additional wine drunk during the meal — only if he intended so beforehand.
Changing his mind without prior intent, or receiving wine from others — he must recite the berachah again.

paragraphs: En lebarek beraka acharona al hayyayin shel qiddush shehu bimqom seuda, o al hayyayin sheshshoteh qodem shear seuda ubeezeh zeman sheyyihyeh v"p sheeno shoteh yayin betok hasseuda, debirkat hammazon poteret beraka acharona shel hayyayin sheshshata qodem seuda, abal im akal mine mezonot qodem birkat hammotzi yebarek beraka meen shalosh qodem netilat yadayim sheqqodem hammotzi, velo yismok al birkat hammazon lekattechilla, veim lo berak beraka acharona qodem hammotzi venizkar achar shebberak hammotzi lo yebarek beraka acharona al mine mezonot sheakal qodem hammotzi, raq yekavven lepateram bebirkat hammazon:

Vekol zeh davqa bemine mezonot, abal im akal perot o shata mashqin qodem birkat hammotzi veshakach velo berek beraka acharona qodem netilat yadayim vehammotzi venizkar achar birkat hammotzi yebarek beraka acharona apillu beemtza seuda, mippene sheen birkat hammazon poteret ella midi dezin udebarim habbaim betok hasseuda veayyen acharonim:

clarification.explanation: One does not recite a concluding berachah over the wine of Kiddush (which comes in place of a meal) or over wine drunk before the meal, because Birkat HaMazon exempts it. But if he ate mezonot foods (cake and the like) before Hamotzi, he should recite a berachah me'ein shalosh before netilat yadayim, and should not rely on Birkat HaMazon from the outset; and if he forgot and remembered only after Hamotzi, he should no longer recite a berachah, but should intend to exempt them through Birkat HaMazon. But fruits and beverages eaten or drunk before Hamotzi that he forgot to recite a concluding berachah over — if he remembers after Hamotzi, he recites a concluding berachah over them even in the middle of the meal, because Birkat HaMazon exempts only things that are within the meal itself.
takeaways: Kiddush wine and mezonot foods that were forgotten — are exempted by Birkat HaMazon.
Fruits/beverages forgotten before Hamotzi — one recites a concluding berachah over them even in the middle of the meal.

paragraphs: Im betok hasseuda shoteh mayim yesh omerim dimbarek alehem, veyesh omerim deeno mebarek veqayma lan sapeq berakot lehaqel velo yebarek ella yeharher habberaka belibbo, o yomar berik rachamana shehakkol nihya bidbaro, al ken kede lehistalleq min hassapeq hazzeh deikka ben happoseqin hannizkar - yesheb qodem netila bimqom seuda veyishteh mayim vibarek alayv al daat liptor kol mah sheyyishteh betok seuddato, ak yizzaher sheyyishteh pachot mishshiur kede shello yitchayyeb beraka acharona, yaan sheim yebarek beraka acharona lo hoil betaqqanato kelum, deatta lo yukal liptor beotah beraka lemah sheshshoteh betok hasseuda, vegam yizzaher shello yetze chutza achar sheyyishteh mishshum dehammishna meqomo tzarik lachazor ulebarek keshechozer limqomo venimtza shello hoil betaqqanato veken katab rabbenu mh"r chayyim veyittol za"l taqqana zo dishtiyyat hammayim vehizhir sheyyishteh pachot mishshiur kede shello yitchayyeb bibraka acharona, veim yesh yayin betok hasseuda eno tzarik lekol zeh, ki birkat hayyayin poteret kol mine mashqim vekannizkar beshaar taame hammitzot:

Vehinneh tiqqun zeh shehu lishtot mayim qodem hammotzi lo epshar laasoto bekol et, yaan ki lipamim en haadam taeb lemayim qodem hammotzi kelal, vekol sheeno tzame veeno taeb lammayim kelal yesh lehistappeq im muttar lo laasot ken ulebarek alehem, vahagam deyesh metayyeri lehedya bikhay gavna shehu mebarek kede liptor hammayim shebbetok hasseuda, im kol zeh en haddabar barur etzlenu veen leadam lehaknis atzmo besapeq gabbe berakot, veayyen chesed laalapim siman q"d ot d' behaggahat "mar bereh derabina" za"l yeuyyan sham, al ken im lo yihyeh tzame velo haya taeb lammayim kelal o shekkebar natal yadayv velo asa tiqqun hannizkar shel shetiyyat hammayim, yizzaher lebarek shehakkol al chatikat sukkar vekaddomeh betok hasseuda qodem sheyyishteh hammayim vekivven liptor et hammayim sheyyishteh, vekak haya minhago shel ateret rashe harab mor abi zlh"h lebarek al mine metiqa tamid qodem sheyyishteh mayim betok hasseuda vehaya nizhar bazeh meod, velaken kol adam nakon lehizzaher bazeh, umihu bishte seudot shel shabbat shemmeqaddesh bahem al hayyayin eno tzarik lehizzaher bekol zeh, ki birkat hayyayin shel qiddush shehu bimqom seuda poteret kol mashqin shebbetok hasseuda, vetzarik sheyyekavven bebirkat hayyayin shel qiddush liptor hammayim shebbetok hasseuda, veayyen tzappichit bidbash siman v' ayyen sham, veyesh medaqdeqin lomar qodem qiddush deshabbat achar sheomerim leshem yichud veku' vahareni mekavven liptor bibraka sheabarek al yayin deqiddush et kol mine mashqin sheeshteh betok hasseuda, uminhag zeh nakon hu ki haadam alul leshikcha ubazeh nimtza hu zariz veniskar:

clarification.explanation:
One who drinks water during the meal — there are those who say he recites a berachah over it, and those who say he does not; and since in doubtful cases regarding berachot we are lenient, he should not recite a berachah, but should contemplate the berachah in his heart or say "Blessed is the Merciful One, by Whose word all things came to be." To remove himself from this doubt, he should sit before netilat yadayim in the place of the meal, drink water, and recite a berachah over it with the intent of exempting everything he will drink during the meal; but he must be careful to drink less than the required measure, so as not to become obligated in a concluding berachah (for if he recites a concluding berachah, the remedy is nullified), and not to go outside afterward (since one who changes his place must recite the berachah again). So wrote Rav Chaim Vital, may his memory be blessed. And if there is wine at the meal, none of this is necessary, since the berachah on wine exempts all beverages.
However, this remedy (drinking water before Hamotzi) is not always possible, since sometimes one is not thirsty at all; and one who is not thirsty should doubt whether it is permitted for him to recite a berachah over the water, and one should not place oneself in doubt. Therefore, if he is not thirsty, or has already washed his hands and did not perform the remedy, he should recite Shehakol over a piece of sugar or the like during the meal before drinking, and intend to exempt the water (and such was the custom of the Ben Ish Chai's father, to be very careful about this). And at the two Shabbat meals at which one recites Kiddush over wine, none of this is necessary, since the berachah on the Kiddush wine (which is in place of a meal) exempts all beverages; and he should intend in it to exempt the water. And there are those who are precise to say this explicitly before Kiddush — and this is a proper custom, since a person is prone to forget.
takeaways: Water during the meal — it is doubtful whether one recites a berachah over it, and doubtful berachot are treated leniently; one should not recite a berachah but should contemplate it or say "Blessed is the Merciful One, by Whose word all things came to be."

Remedy: drink water before netilat yadayim and recite a berachah with intent to exempt (less than the required measure, and without going outside afterward); and if not thirsty — recite Shehakol over sugar to exempt.
At Kiddush over wine — the berachah on the wine exempts the water; one should intend this in it (and some are accustomed to say this explicitly).

paragraphs: Shekar sheshshotin betok hasseuda im shotehu leorer taavat hammaakol hare hu tapel lasseuda veen tzarik lebarek alayv, veim shotehu lechammem haitztomeka leakkel hammaakol tzarik lebarek alayv, umihu kevan deharbeh peamim timtza kavvanat haadam hi leorer bo taavat hammaakol, qasheh haddabar lemeqam alah demilleta bekavvanat hashshotehu veal harob mekavven leha uleha veqayma lan sapeq berakot lehaqel lekak lo yebarek alayv, umah gam od belav haki habberaka al hassakar enah berura etzel kol adam yaan ki hu sorep haggaron, veyesh kamma bene adam hu lahem keqotz makib umechamat ken nohagim lishtot acharayv mayim tekep umiyyad, veal ken tob lehizzaher leekol dabar shebbirkato shehakkol kemo sukkar vekayyotze qodem sheyyishteh hashshekar vikavven liptor hashshekar, vezakur lattob harab adoni abi zlh"h shemmemayv lo berak al hashshekar ella haya loqeach chatikat sukkar umebarek lepatero, vaapillu im shoteh bayyom kos qatan shel shekar leezeh tzorek, sheeno bishat seuda, haya darko lebarek techilla al chatikat sukkar ki haya mezumman etzlo baabur dabar zeh, ukebar amarnu shebbisudat shabbat veyom tob shemmeqaddeshim al hayyayin en tzarik laasot tiqqun ki birkat hayyayin shel qiddush poteret kol mashqin, lekak yekavven haadam liptor bo mayim veshekar vekol mine mashqin:

clarification.explanation: Beer (an intoxicating beverage) drunk during the meal: if one drinks it to arouse appetite — it is secondary to the meal and one does not recite a berachah over it; and if one drinks it to warm the stomach and digest the food — one must recite a berachah. But since it is difficult to know clearly the drinker's intent (usually both intentions are mixed together), the halachah follows the principle that in doubtful cases regarding berachot we are lenient — so one should not recite a berachah over it alone. Therefore it is good to eat something whose berachah is Shehakol (such as sugar) before drinking the beer and intend to exempt it; and at Shabbat/Yom Tov meals with Kiddush over wine — this is not necessary, since the berachah on the wine exempts everything. This advice is correct not only during the meal: the Ben Ish Chai testifies that his father, may his memory be blessed, always practiced this — even when he drank a small cup of beer during the day for some purpose not at the time of a meal at all, he would recite a berachah first over a piece of sugar that he kept ready for this purpose, and thereby exempt the beer.
takeaways: Beer during the meal — a doubtful berachah, therefore one does not recite a berachah over it alone.
One exempts it with the berachah of Shehakol over sugar beforehand, or with the berachah on the Kiddush wine.
The practice of reciting Shehakol over sugar before beer is good to follow even not at the time of a meal — every time one drinks a cup of beer during the day.

paragraphs: Debarim habbaim betok hasseuda, im baim mechamat hasseuda dehaynu shehem debarim shedderek liqboa seuda alehem, ben shebbaim laleket bahem et happat kegon basar vedagim viraqot ugebina ubetzim umine meluchim ben shehem baim lehazin ulehasbia kegon mine tabshilin maaseh qedera sheen baim kede lelappet bahem happat ella kede lehazin ulehasbia, hare ellu enam tzerikin beraka lipnehem apillu sheokelam belo pat, mishshum debirkat hammotzi potartam, veenam tzerikin beraka leacharehem debirkat hammazon potartam, yaan dibellu en darkam leekol otam kol hayyom kemo happerot ella raq bishat seuda bilbad, ulekak hem tepelim lappat shehu iqqar hasseuda veniptarim bebirkat happat "p sheokelam belo pat: vekol mine perot habbaim betok hasseuda im okelam im happat en tzarik beraka kelal, mishshum dekevan deatta okelam im happat naasu tepelim lappat ubirkat hammotzi potartan, abal im en okel otam im happat ella okelam lebaddam bigmar hasseuda leqinnucha vetaanug bealema, hare ellu tzerikin beraka lipnehem veen niptarin bebirkat hammotzi, kevan sheenam meiqqar hahisuda vedarkam leakelam kol hayyom apillu shello bishat seuda, abal en teunin beraka leacharehem mishshum kevan debau tok hasseuda qodem sheyyimmasheku yedehem min happat birkat hammazon potartan, dekol mah shebba tok hasseuda hu mikkelal hassebia shenneemar bah veakalta vesabaetta uberakta ukemo shekkatub beshulchan aruk lehaggaon rabbenu zalman za"l:

clarification.explanation: Foods that come during the meal on account of the meal — whether those eaten as a relish with the bread (meat, fish, vegetables, cheese, eggs, salted foods) or those that come to nourish and satiate (cooked pot dishes) — do not require a berachah before or after them, even if eaten without bread, because the berachah of Hamotzi and Birkat HaMazon exempt them (since they are customarily eaten only at the time of a meal, unlike fruits eaten all day). Likewise, fruits eaten with the bread do not require a berachah, since they have become secondary to the bread; but if eaten alone at the end of the meal for dessert and enjoyment, they require an opening berachah (since they are not part of the essence of the meal and are also eaten not at the time of a meal), but they do not require a concluding berachah, since everything that comes during the meal is included in the satiety that Birkat HaMazon exempts.
takeaways: Foods that serve as a relish for bread or that satiate — are exempt from a berachah (even without bread).
Fruits eaten separately for dessert — require an opening berachah, but not a concluding one (Birkat HaMazon exempts it).

paragraphs: Im qaba liptan seuddato al dabar acher, vehebiu lepanayv perot gam ken veokel qetzatam im pat uqetzatam belo pat, hinneh yesh bazeh deot chaluqot veyesh omerim kol shehu melappet bahem happat techilla vesop ap al gab deokel benetayim belo pat hare ellu niptarim bebirkat hammotzi, veyesh omerim apillu im melappet bahem pat techilla vesop meachar sheokel benetayim belo pat en niptarim bebirkat hammotzi, yaan ki hu lo qaba seuddato alehem lelappet bahem happat ki yesh lo dabar acher lelappet bo, veal ken kede latzet yede hammachaloqet katebu haacharonim za"l im rotzeh leekol qetzatam bepat uqetzatam belo pat yaaseh kak yokal techilla meat belo pat vibarek alehem, veaach"k yoklem ben bepat ben belo pat, vedin zeh eno ella beqobea seuddato al shear debarim ella sherotzeh lelappet happat gam im qetzat perot, abal im hu beemet qobea seuddato al happerot lelappet bahem happat az yokal techilla pat im happerot velo yebarek al happerot, veaach"k im yokal qetzat mehem belo pat gam ken lo yebarek, mihu tob lehizzaher sheyyallepet happat bahem gam lebassop veayyen acharonim za"l: velaken otam hannohagim bime haqqayitz leekol pat ugebina ak okelim immahem qishshuin o abattichim vehem osin kol hallipot bigbina, veraq ben kol leyappot shettayim veshalosh chatikot shel gebina loqechim chatikat qishshuim o haabattichim belo leyappot pat kede lematteq akilato mimmelichot haggebina, hinneh hem tzerikin lehizzaher leekol techilla min haqqishshuin o haabattichim im happat vegam lebassop gam ken yizzaharu lelappet bahem happat, veaz benetayim yekolim leekol kamma chatikot mehem bezeh achar zeh belo leyappot pat, vehayyoter nakon hu laasot kak sheyyokal mehem chatika achat qodem netilat yadayim vibarek al daat liptor mah sheyyokal mehem betok hasseuda vahare zeh okel mehem betok hasseuda belo leyappot beli piqpuq veayyen acharonim:

clarification.explanation:
One who made his meal's basis upon something other than fruit, and fruits were also brought before him, and he eats some of them with bread and some without bread — there is a dispute about this: some say that as long as he uses them as a relish with the bread at the beginning and the end, even though he eats some in between without bread, they are exempted by the berachah of Hamotzi; and some say that even if he uses them as a relish with bread at the beginning and the end, since he eats some in between without bread, they are not exempted (since he did not make his meal's basis upon them). Therefore, to satisfy both views, the acharonim wrote: if one wishes to eat some of them with bread and some without, he should eat a little of them first without bread and recite a berachah over them first, and afterward eat them either with or without bread.
All this applies when one has made his meal's basis upon other things and merely wishes to also use a little fruit as a relish with bread; but if he has truly made his meal's basis upon the fruit itself, to use it as a relish with the bread — he should eat bread with the fruit first without reciting a berachah over the fruit (and it is good to also use it as a relish with bread again at the end). Therefore, those accustomed in the summer to eat bread and cheese together with cucumbers or watermelons, doing all their "relish" with the cheese, and only in between, between two or three pieces of cheese, taking a piece of cucumber or watermelon without using bread as a relish, to sweeten their eating from the saltiness of the cheese — must be careful to eat first from the cucumbers or watermelons with bread, and also be careful to use them as a relish with bread at the end; and the most correct practice is to eat a piece of them before netilat yadayim and recite a berachah with intent to exempt whatever he eats of them during the meal.
takeaways: One who made his meal's basis upon something else and eats fruit partly with bread and partly without — there is a dispute whether it is exempted by Hamotzi.
To resolve the doubt: eat a little of it without bread and recite the berachah first, and then eat as one wishes; or recite a berachah over a piece before netilat yadayim to exempt it.
One who made his meal's basis upon the fruit itself — should eat it with bread first without a berachah (and use it as a relish with bread again at the end).

paragraphs: Katab bechesed laalapim q"z ot v' perot mebushshalim beenayhu, apillu im habbasar im i hatchalat qebiut seuddato alehem yesh mi sheomer shetztzarik lebarek alehem veken beqishshuim kebushim vekaddomeh, veyesh mi sheomer daapillu okelam im happat tzarik lebarek, veyesh mi sheomer sheen lebarek kevan shebbaim letzorek seuda velo leqinnucha, ulekak yere shamayim yesheb qodem seuda vibarek al min oto peri veyokal pachot mikkashshiur vikavven liptor - ad kan leshono, veim i epshar lo behaki ubiprat im hu oreach az yeharher habberaka belibbo, o yomar berik rachamana ubiprat im hu oreach az yeharher habberaka belibbo, o yomar berik rachamana bore peri haadama o bore peri haetz kepi mah shehu happeri:

clarification.explanation: Cooked fruits as they are — even together with meat — if they were not present from the beginning of the meal's basis, there is one who says one must recite a berachah over them, and likewise regarding pickled cucumbers and the like; and there is one who says that even eating them with bread requires a berachah; and there is one who says one should not recite a berachah, since they come for the purpose of the meal and not for dessert (Chesed LaAlafim). Therefore one who fears Heaven should sit before the meal and recite a berachah over that type of fruit, and eat less than the required measure, intending to exempt. And if this is not possible for him — particularly if he is a guest — he should contemplate the berachah in his heart, or say "Blessed is the Merciful One, Creator of the fruit of the earth" or "Creator of the fruit of the tree," according to what the fruit is.
takeaways: Cooked or pickled fruits brought during the meal — there is a dispute whether one recites a berachah over them (even with bread).

One who fears Heaven should recite a berachah over them before the meal (less than the required measure) to exempt; and if not possible — contemplate it in his heart, or say "Blessed is the Merciful One, Creator of the fruit of the earth/tree."

paragraphs: Bisudat lel shabbat darkan shel bene adam lehaarik al hashshulchan shalosh vearba shaot ubiprat bime hachoretz, uminhagam kak achar birkat hammotzi okelin mine meluchin bechometz, veokelin hattabshilin shel basar maaseh qedera shebbishshelu likbod shabbat, veaach"k mesirin hattabshil umebiim mine perot umannichin al hashshulchan umebarekim alehem umaarikin al hashshulchan b' veg' shaot ad sheyyebareku birkat hammazon, ak darkan lehashir pat al hashshulchan ad birkat hammazon kede shennireh sheadayin lo masheku yedehem min happat, sheim masheku yedehem min happat hayu tzerikin lebarek al kol mah shebbeyaim ben im hem debarim habbain mechamat hasseuda kegon dagim vekayyotze, ben mine perot dilpum dati tzarik lebarek lipnehem uleacharehem deen potartam birkat hammotzi velo birkat hammazon kevan dehebium achar shemmasheku yedehem min happat, al ken hem nizharim lehannicha perusat pat al hashshulchan kede shennireh shello masheku yedehem min happat, veaz lo yihyu nirin kemoilin bibrakot kesheen mebarekin alehem, mihu "p shehappat odennu munnach al hashshulchan ad birkat hammazon yere shamayim yizzaher leekol meat min happat samuk mammash lintilat mayim acharonim, vegam beet sheorekin happerot al hashshulchan gam ken yokal meat min happat debazeh nimtza beemet shello mashak yado min happat, veetzlenu bebetenu minhag shellanu lehabi gam bisuda rishona useuda sheniyya shel shabbat dagim veneekol mehem meat im happat samuk lintilat mayim acharonim vehu minhag yapeh venakon, denimtza bekol meshek shettayim veshalosh shaot sheanachnu yoshebim al hashshulchan hearuk mipperot en anachnu moshekim yadenu mehappat, shebbedatenu leekol od mehappat im haddagim shenneekol lebassop:

clarification.explanation: At the Friday night meal it is customary to linger at the table for many hours: one eats salted foods in vinegar, meat dishes, and afterward the cooked dish is removed and fruits are brought. It became customary to leave a slice of bread on the table until Birkat HaMazon, so that it should appear one has not "withdrawn his hands from the bread" — for if one had withdrawn his hands, he would need to recite a berachah over everything brought afterward (both meal-items and fruit). Therefore, even though the bread remains on the table, one who fears Heaven should be careful to taste a little bread very close to the end, and likewise when the fruits are arranged on the table — so that he truly does not withdraw his hand from the bread.
takeaways: It is customary to leave bread on the table throughout the meal (as a sign that one's "hands were not withdrawn" from it).
It is good to taste a little bread very close to the end, so as to actually maintain the continuity of eating bread.

paragraphs: Im akal tabshil shel qishshuin o kabush shel qishshuin vekayyotze betok hasseuda shello berek alayv, veachar gemar hasseuda qodem birkat hammazon areku lepanayv perot leqinnucha vetaanug ubiklalam hebiu gam ken qishshuin chayyin, yesh omerim shetztzarik lebarek alehem veyesh omerim sheen tzarik lebarek, veal ken yere shamayim yokal min acher asher birkato shaveh im zeh hammin vibarek alayv veyiptor gam et zeh, o qodem sheyyokal hattabshil vehakkibbush yiqqach chatika mizzeh hammin velo yokal mimmennu atta kede shello yaknis atzmo biplugta dibrakot. abal en lo taqqana lomar yokal viharher habberaka belibbo deen omerim ken ella beones ubedochaq veayyen zekor leyitzchaq harari za"l siman mch yeuyyan sham. veim yimtza adam acher leekol ulebarek vikavven alayv hinneh mah tob:

clarification.explanation: One who ate, during the meal, a cooked dish of cucumbers or pickled cucumbers without reciting a berachah over them, and afterward (before Birkat HaMazon) fruits were brought to him for dessert, among them raw cucumbers — there is a dispute whether one must recite a berachah over them: some say yes, some say no. Therefore one who fears Heaven should follow one of two paths in order not to enter into doubt: eat another type whose berachah is identical to that of cucumbers and recite a berachah over it with intent to also exempt the cucumbers; or, before eating the cooked dish or the pickled item at the beginning of the meal, take for himself a piece of a raw cucumber and not eat it yet (so that it remains requiring a berachah later, and he does not enter into doubt). A third, even better way: if he can find another person who will eat some of those cucumbers and recite a berachah over them, intending to also exempt him — that is very good. One should not rely merely on contemplating the berachah in his heart, for that is resorted to only in a case of unavoidable circumstance and real difficulty.
takeaways: Raw cucumbers brought for dessert after cooked cucumbers were eaten without a berachah — there is a dispute whether they require a berachah.
The solution: recite a berachah over another type with an identical berachah, intending to exempt it as well; or set aside a piece of cucumber in advance and not eat it.
Another good option: find another person to eat and recite a berachah over the cucumbers, intending to exempt him too.

paragraphs: Yere shamayim yizzaher bekol seuda beshaa shemmebarek lihyot dato al kol sheyyabo lo apillu bederek rechoqa deeno orecha demilleta, yaan deyesh omerim im achar shebberak al happat shalechu lo doron mibbet acherim velo haya dato al haddoron, az apillu im hu middebarim sheddarkan lelappet bahem happat im kol zeh im eno okelam im happat tzarik lebarek alehem kedin nimlak, veyesh omerim sheen tzarik lebarek distam daat haadam al kol mah shemmebiin lo bisuda, lekak hannizhar lihyot dato beshaa shemmebarek al happat veal hayyayin veal happerot al kol mah sheyyabiu lo, hen bederek doron vaapillu mimmaqom rachoq hare hu nitztzol missela hammachleqot hannizkeret, vealayv tabo birkat tob:

clarification.explanation: One who fears Heaven should be careful at every meal, at the time he recites the berachah, to have his mind on everything that may come to him — even in a far-fetched way that is not usual. The reason: there are those who say that if, after he recited a berachah over the bread, a gift was sent to him from another's house and he had not had it in mind, then even if it is of the type ordinarily used as a relish with bread — if he does not eat it with bread, he must recite a berachah over it, in the law of one who changes his mind; and there are those who say he need not recite a berachah, since a person's mind is ordinarily set on everything brought to him at the meal. Therefore, one who is careful to have in mind, at the time he recites the berachah over the bread, the wine, and the fruit, everything that will be brought to him — even as a gift and from a distant place — is saved from this dispute, and blessing will come upon him.
takeaways: At the time of the berachah, intend everything that will come during the meal, even a gift arriving from far away.
A gift that arrives after the berachah, which was not intended — there is a dispute whether one must recite a berachah over it; one who intends everything in advance is saved from the doubt.
